title: Planar kernel: single-pass arrangement merges non-adjacent same-color bands across multiple parallel dividers (latent, product-unreachable)
description:
LATENT planar-kernel topology quirk independently found + proven by two P3-QA agents. Real kernel-correctness gap, but CURRENTLY PRODUCT-UNREACHABLE. No code changed — filed for tracking.

SYMPTOM
The single-pass arrangement builder buildArrangementFromShapes (packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts, calling packages/core/src/engine/planar/arrangement.ts) merges TWO NON-ADJACENT SAME-COLOR fill bands into ONE face when a same-color fill is crossed by MULTIPLE PARALLEL full-crossing stroke dividers.

REPRO (re-confirmed in a scratch vitest using the planar.test.ts rectShape/strokeLineShape helpers; scratch removed, tree clean):
  buildArrangementFromShapes([
    rectShape (single same-color RED fill, full width, e.g. ~90px wide),
    strokeLineShape (divider 1, fully crossing the rect),
    strokeLineShape (divider 2, parallel, fully crossing the rect),
  ])
With a ~90px-wide rect whose area is 9000 → bounded filled faces come back as [6000, 3000] (2 faces) instead of [3000, 3000, 3000] (3 faces). eulerCharacteristic(ps) = -1 (a stray bridge edge; should be the planar value for 3 disjoint bands). The two OUTER bands (top + bottom), which are NON-ADJACENT, are wrongly fused through the middle band's span into one 6000-area face while the middle band is correct. (Also reproduced at 30px×100px = area 3000 → [2000,1000], euler -1: the two outer thirds fuse to 2000, middle third correct at 1000.)

CONTRAST (works): DISTINCT-color abutting bands split correctly into 3/4 separate faces. The bug is SPECIFIC to same-color multi-divider geometry — the same-fill style-dedup that should keep regions separate when a stroke divider lies between them instead lets non-adjacent same-fill bands seam back together across the middle divider.

NOT A REGRESSION
This is PRE-EXISTING in the P0/P1 arrangement builder (arrangement.ts / build.ts). It was NOT introduced by P3 (task 1321 only touched query.ts / split.ts / subselection.ts / live.ts; it did not modify the single-pass build path).

CURRENTLY PRODUCT-UNREACHABLE
The live editing path does NOT call buildArrangementFromShapes single-pass on this geometry. Live shape commits use the INCREMENTAL fold (commitMergeShape / foldShapeIntoLayer), which produces 3 separate explicit closed fill loops; livePlanarShape then rebuilds 3 correct selectable faces. So partial-region selection + split-on-move work correctly today (proven via e2e: extracting the middle band leaves both outer bands intact). The quirk only manifests if buildArrangementFromShapes is run on such geometry FROM SCRATCH.

INERT TODAY
Area-conserving (the same-color bands union back via dissolvable seams; total area is preserved) and PUBLISH-INERT — golden-parity self-determinism hash 9d09912df4727d0c is unchanged (the SWF compiler has no path through the single-pass build).

WHY FILE DESPITE BEING INERT
It is a real kernel correctness gap: the arrangement SHOULD yield 3 faces for 3 same-color bands separated by 2 stroke dividers. A future phase (P4 eraser-split / P5, or any new code that rebuilds an arrangement single-pass) could expose it. Tracking it now so it isn't dismissed-and-forgotten — we have TWICE had a 'flagged geometry seam rated inert' turn out to be a real bug (tasks 1316/1317).

FILE LOCATIONS
  packages/core/src/engine/planar/build.ts   (buildArrangementFromShapes; single-pass entry)
  packages/core/src/engine/planar/arrangement.ts  (Arrangement build / face extraction)

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
The single-pass face-extraction / seam-dissolve logic must keep NON-ADJACENT same-fill bands SEPARATE when a stroke divider lies between them. Same intent as P2's seamDissolvable rule (a same-fill interior seam dissolves only when it carries NO stroke) but applied in the BUILD path: a same-fill seam that coincides with (or is bridged through) a full-crossing stroke divider must NOT dissolve, so the outer bands stay distinct faces. Add adversarial regression tests (same-color rect + N parallel full-crossing dividers → N+1 faces, euler == expected planar value, areas conserved AND equal-per-band).
